context: Request: stale-pipeline review as of August 6, 2026: commercial deals signed on or before May 8, 2026 that have not closed. Rubric: nine qualifying matters of mixed types (1004-00003, 1009-00006, 1013-00001, 1017-00001, 1019-00002, 1027-00002, 1029-00001, 1036-00005, 1038-00009) and a precision criterion.

stages.stage: List files in the document store
stages.note: Whole-store glob; the summary names three high-numbered matters as the deal candidates.

stages.stage: List matter folders
stages.note: Lists all matter folders with file counts.

stages.stage: Search file names for request keywords
stages.note: File-name sweep for deal, agreement, signing and closing words prints about 213K chars; the summary keeps three recent matters. The review flags candidates chosen by recency without paging.

stages.stage: Search file names for request keywords
stages.note: Attempt 2: heredoc error, then a per-matter table of signing, closing and termination file-name counts (338 lines to a file); concludes one recent matter is the only pending one. The review flags the narrow signing filter.

stages.stage: Scan document text with an extraction script
stages.note: Store-wide text scan for 2026 dates and pending-closing phrases times out; the rerun covers only the six highest number prefixes (about 99K chars). The review flags that the rest of the store was never scanned.

stages.stage: Screen candidate matters by reading documents
stages.note: declared: Read documents picked from the file listing. Reads ten executed agreements, checklists and emails of four high-numbered candidates; the review flags the four-matter set.

stages.stage: Calculate figures for the answer
stages.note: Day counts from four signing dates to the as-of date.

stages.stage: Write the response
stages.note: Writes one signed financing commitment as the only stale deal, with exclusions; the review flags single-matter answers and possibly misapplied exclusions.

stages.stage: Check or revise the response
stages.note: Re-reads the response, checks cited paths, two wording edits.

stages.stage: Finish the run
stages.note: Calls finish.

runs.sequence: List files in the document store → List matter folders → Search file names for request keywords → Scan document text with an extraction script → Screen candidate matters by reading documents → Calculate figures for the answer → Write the response → Check or revise the response → Finish the run
runs.failure_point: After its store-wide text scan timed out it rescanned only the newest matter-number prefixes, so none of the older signed-but-unclosed deals were ever opened, and it answered with one recent financing commitment.

first_error.stage: Scan document text with an extraction script
first_error.why: After the store-wide scan timed out the agent reran it only over the six highest number prefixes, which hold none of the needed matters, and never scanned or searched the rest another way; the earlier file-name sweeps had listed them only inside 200K-character noise.
first_error.critic_note: (specific flag) The scan review said the rescan was limited to the highest prefixes so the rest of the store was never scanned, naming one needed matter among the unopened; the agent went on to read four recent matters.

other_errors.why: The answer flags a signed financing commitment letter as the one stale deal, a matter outside the qualifying set (evidence seen at [38]-[48]).
other_errors.critic_note: Reviews asked to confirm whether it had closed, not whether a commitment letter counts as a signed deal.

runs.failure_point: Its store-wide text scans kept timing out; it moved on with a narrow, capped file-name grep that reached one of the nine qualifying deals, and its answer added matters with stale status evidence.

first_error.stage: Search file names for request keywords
first_error.why: With the background scans still running and only one prefix scanned, the agent built its candidate list from a capped file-name grep for status and delay words that reached only one of the needed matters, and never returned to the scans or the earlier broad file-name lists.
first_error.critic_note: (specific flag) The review of this stage said the scans had produced no output, the file-name filter was narrow and capped, and the nine candidates were hand-picked; the agent went straight to reading them.

other_errors.why: The answer flags a deal whose only status records were from the year before as still unclosed and lists a terminated deal as meeting the literal test (evidence seen at [81]-[101]).
other_errors.critic_note: (specific flag) The read review at [103] named the stale 2023-2025 status evidence for that matter, and the write review flagged the terminated extras; the check stages kept both.

runs.failure_point: Its text scans were keyed on M&A agreement file names and one timed out with only the tail viewed, so most qualifying deals of other types never surfaced; four that did surface were not opened, and the answer added a deal that had closed.

first_error.stage: Scan document text with an extraction script
first_error.why: The per-matter summary kept the scan's filter on M&A agreement file names, timed out and was read only from its last 50 lines, and the agent neither reran nor broadened it, so the financing, investment and other deal types among the needed matters never surfaced.
first_error.critic_note: (specific flag) The reviews at [23] and [31] named the deal-agreement file-name filter, the unread output and the partial coverage; the agent kept the filter and moved to screening.

other_errors.stage: Screen candidate matters by reading documents
other_errors.why: Four needed matters appeared in the summary lines shown at [29], but when choosing ten candidates to list and read the agent left them out and never opened them.
other_errors.critic_note: (generic flag) The screening reviews listed about 60 unopened surfaced matters without singling these out.

other_errors.why: The answer flags a deal as still unclosed from a pre-closing tracker of the year before, a matter outside the qualifying set (evidence seen at [66]-[82]).
other_errors.critic_note: (specific flag) The review at [106] doubted that matter's fit and asked to verify its closing status; the agent wrote it as stale without new evidence.

divergence: All fail, the same way at heart: the store-wide text scan that was each run's route to signed-but-unclosed deals timed out or was filtered (T0 rescanned only the highest number prefixes, T1 abandoned running background scans for a capped file-name grep, T2 kept a filter on M&A agreement file names and read only the tail of a timed-out summary). The broad file-name sweeps had listed every needed matter but inside 130-210K characters of noise. In each run the scan review named the coverage problem specifically and the agent moved on. T1 and T2 then found the one needed acquisition and scored 1/10; all three answers added non-qualifying matters (a financing commitment in T0, deals with stale pre-closing records in T1 and T2).
